segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Santuṭṭhasutta
segs.e: Content

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ viharati.
segs.e: At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Santuṭṭhāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī;
segs.e: “Mendicants, Kassapa is content with any kind of robe, and praises such contentment.

segs.p: na ca cīvarahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca cīvaraṁ na paritassati; laddhā ca cīvaraṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: He doesn’t employ improper solicitation for the sake of a robe. He doesn’t worry if he doesn’t get a robe. And if he does get a robe, he uses it untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawback, and understanding the escape.

segs.p: Santuṭṭhāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena piṇḍapātena, itarītarapiṇḍapātasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca piṇḍapātahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca piṇḍapātaṁ na paritassati; laddhā ca piṇḍapātaṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: Kassapa is content with any kind of almsfood …

segs.p: Santuṭṭhāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena senāsanena, itarītarasenāsanasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca senāsanahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca senāsanaṁ na paritassati; laddhā ca senāsanaṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: Kassapa is content with any kind of lodging …

segs.p: Santuṭṭhāyaṁ, bhikkhave, kassapo itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, itarītaragilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī; na ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ na paritassati; laddhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: Kassapa is content with any kind of medicines and supplies for the sick …

segs.p: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ: ‘santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādino; na ca cīvarahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjissāma;
segs.e: So you should train like this: ‘We will be content with any kind of robe, and praise such contentment. We won’t employ improper solicitation for the sake of a robe.

segs.p: aladdhā ca cīvaraṁ na ca paritassissāma; laddhā ca cīvaraṁ agadhitā amucchitā anajjhāpannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjissāma’.
segs.e: We won’t worry if we don’t get a robe. And if we do get a robe, we’ll use it untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawback, and understanding the escape.’

segs.p: (Evaṁ sabbaṁ kātabbaṁ.)
segs.e: (All should be told in full the same way.)

segs.p: ‘Santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena piṇḍapātena …pe…
segs.e: ‘We will be content with any kind of almsfood …’

segs.p: santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena senāsanena …pe…
segs.e: ‘We will be content with any kind of lodging …’

segs.p: santuṭṭhā bhavissāma itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, itarītaragilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādino; na ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjissāma aladdhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ na paritassissāma; laddhā ca gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ agadhitā amucchitā anajjhāpannā ādīnavadassāvino nissaraṇapaññā paribhuñjissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will be content with any kind of medicines and supplies for the sick …’

segs.p: Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Kassapena vā hi vo, bhikkhave, ovadissāmi yo vā panassa kassapasadiso, ovaditehi ca pana vo tathattāya paṭipajjitabban”ti.
segs.e: I will exhort you with the example of Kassapa or someone like him. You should practice accordingly.”

segs.p: Paṭhamaṁ.

segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Anottappīsutta
segs.e: Imprudent

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca sāriputto bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākassapa and Venerable Sāriputta were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākassapena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Mahākassapa, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Mahākassapa:

segs.p: “vuccati hidaṁ, āvuso kassapa, anātāpī anottappī abhabbo sambodhāya abhabbo nibbānāya abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya;
segs.e: “Reverend Kassapa, it’s said that without being keen and prudent you can’t achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: ātāpī ca kho ottappī bhabbo sambodhāya bhabbo nibbānāya bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti.
segs.e: But if you are keen and prudent you can achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: “Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, anātāpī hoti anottappī abhabbo sambodhāya abhabbo nibbānāya abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya;
segs.e: To what extent is this the case?”

segs.p: kittāvatā ca panāvuso, ātāpī hoti ottappī bhabbo sambodhāya bhabbo nibbānāya bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti?

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ātappaṁ karoti, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ātappaṁ karoti, ‘anuppannā me kusalā dhammā nuppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ātappaṁ karoti, ‘uppannā me kusalā dhammā nirujjhamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ātappaṁ karoti.
segs.e: “Reverend, take a mendicant who doesn’t foster keenness by thinking: ‘If unarisen unskillful qualities arise in me, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give up arisen unskillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give rise to unarisen skillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If arisen skillful qualities cease in me, they’ll lead to harm.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, anātāpī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how you’re not keen.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, anottappī hoti?
segs.e: And how are you not prudent?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ottappati, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ottappati, ‘anuppannā me kusalā dhammā nuppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ottappati, ‘uppannā me kusalā dhammā nirujjhamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti na ottappati.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who doesn’t foster prudence by thinking: ‘If unarisen unskillful qualities arise in me, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give up arisen unskillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give rise to unarisen skillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If arisen skillful qualities cease in me, they’ll lead to harm.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, anottappī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how you’re not prudent.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, anātāpī anottappī abhabbo sambodhāya abhabbo nibbānāya abhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāya.
segs.e: That’s how without being keen and prudent you can’t achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, ātāpī hoti?
segs.e: And how are you keen?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti ātappaṁ karoti, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti ātappaṁ karoti, anuppannā me kusalā dhammā …pe… ātappaṁ karoti.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who fosters keenness by thinking: ‘If unarisen unskillful qualities arise in me, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give up arisen unskillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give rise to unarisen skillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If arisen skillful qualities cease in me, they’ll lead to harm.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, ātāpī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how you’re keen.

segs.p: Kathañcāvuso, ottappī hoti?
segs.e: And how are you prudent?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘anuppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā uppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti ottappati, ‘uppannā me pāpakā akusalā dhammā appahīyamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti ottappati, ‘anuppannā me kusalā dhammā anuppajjamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti ottappati, ‘uppannā me kusalā dhammā nirujjhamānā anatthāya saṁvatteyyun’ti ottappati.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who fosters prudence by thinking: ‘If unarisen unskillful qualities arise in me, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give up arisen unskillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If I don’t give rise to unarisen skillful qualities, they’ll lead to harm.’ ‘If arisen skillful qualities cease in me, they’ll lead to harm.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, ottappī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how you’re prudent.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, ātāpī ottappī bhabbo sambodhāya bhabbo nibbānāya bhabbo anuttarassa yogakkhemassa adhigamāyā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how if you’re keen and prudent you can achieve awakening, extinguishment, and the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.”

segs.p: Dutiyaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 16.3

segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Candūpamāsutta
segs.e: Like the Moon

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ viharati.
segs.e: At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Candūpamā, bhikkhave, kulāni upasaṅkamatha—
segs.e: “Mendicants, you should approach families like the moon:

segs.p: apakasseva kāyaṁ, apakassa cittaṁ, niccanavakā kulesu appagabbhā.
segs.e: withdrawn in body and mind, ever the newcomer, and never rude.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso jarudapānaṁ vā olokeyya pabbatavisamaṁ vā nadīviduggaṁ vā—
segs.e: Suppose a person were to look down at an old well, a rugged cliff, or an inaccessible riverland.

segs.p: apakasseva kāyaṁ, apakassa cittaṁ;
segs.e: They’d withdraw their body and mind.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, candūpamā kulāni upasaṅkamatha—
segs.e: In the same way, you should approach families like the moon:

segs.p: apakasseva kāyaṁ, apakassa cittaṁ, niccanavakā kulesu appagabbhā.
segs.e: withdrawn in body and mind, always the newcomer, and never rude.

segs.p: Kassapo, bhikkhave, candūpamo kulāni upasaṅkamati—
segs.e: Kassapa approaches families like the moon:

segs.p: apakasseva kāyaṁ, apakassa cittaṁ, niccanavako kulesu appagabbho.
segs.e: withdrawn in body and mind, ever the newcomer, and never rude.

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: kathaṁrūpo bhikkhu arahati kulāni upasaṅkamitun”ti?
segs.e: What kind of mendicant is worthy of approaching families?”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṁnettikā bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṁyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā ākāse pāṇiṁ cālesi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha waved his hand in space.

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṁ ākāse pāṇi na sajjati na gayhati na bajjhati;
segs.e: “Mendicants, this hand is not stuck or held or caught in space.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno kulāni upasaṅkamato kulesu cittaṁ na sajjati na gayhati na bajjhati:
segs.e: In the same way, when approaching families, a mendicant’s mind is not stuck or held or caught, thinking:

segs.p: ‘labhantu lābhakāmā, puññakāmā karontu puññānī’ti;
segs.e: ‘May those who want material things get them, and may those who want merit make merits!’

segs.p: yathāsakena lābhena attamano hoti sumano, evaṁ paresaṁ lābhena attamano hoti sumano;
segs.e: They’re just as pleased and happy when others get something as they are when they get something.

segs.p: evarūpo kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahati kulāni upasaṅkamituṁ.
segs.e: This kind of mendicant is worthy of approaching families.

segs.p: Kassapassa, bhikkhave, kulāni upasaṅkamato kulesu cittaṁ na sajjati na gayhati na bajjhati:
segs.e: When Kassapa approaches families, his mind is not stuck or held or caught, thinking:

segs.p: ‘labhantu lābhakāmā, puññakāmā karontu puññānī’ti;
segs.e: ‘May those who want material things get them, and may those who want merit make merits!’

segs.p: yathāsakena lābhena attamano hoti sumano;
segs.e: He’s just as pleased and happy when others get something as he is when he gets something.

segs.p: evaṁ paresaṁ lābhena attamano hoti sumano.
Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: kathaṁrūpassa bhikkhuno aparisuddhā dhammadesanā hoti, kathaṁrūpassa bhikkhuno parisuddhā dhammadesanā hotī”ti?
segs.e: What kind of mendicant’s teaching is pure, and what kind is impure?”

segs.p: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṁnettikā bhagavaṁpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṁyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. He is our guide and our refuge. Sir, may the Buddha himself please clarify the meaning of this. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, mendicants, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁcitto paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: “Whoever teaches Dhamma to others with the thought:

segs.p: ‘aho vata me dhammaṁ suṇeyyuṁ, sutvā ca pana dhammaṁ pasīdeyyuṁ, pasannā ca me pasannākāraṁ kareyyun’ti;
segs.e: ‘Oh! May they listen to the teaching from me. When they’ve heard it, may they gain confidence in the teaching and demonstrate their confidence to me.’

segs.p: evarūpassa kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno aparisuddhā dhammadesanā hoti.
segs.e: Such a mendicant’s teaching is impure.

segs.p: Yo ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁcitto paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Whoever teaches Dhamma to others with the thought:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhīti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Aho vata me dhammaṁ suṇeyyuṁ, sutvā ca pana dhammaṁ ājāneyyuṁ, ājānitvā ca pana tathattāya paṭipajjeyyun’ti.
segs.e: Oh! May they listen to the teaching from me. When they’ve heard it, may they understand the teaching and practice accordingly.’

segs.p: Iti dhammasudhammataṁ paṭicca paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti, kāruññaṁ paṭicca anuddayaṁ paṭicca anukampaṁ upādāya paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: So they teach others because of the clear rightness of the teaching, out of compassion, kindness, and sympathy.

segs.p: Evarūpassa kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno parisuddhā dhammadesanā hoti.
segs.e: Such a mendicant’s teaching is pure.

segs.p: Kassapo, bhikkhave, evaṁcitto paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti:
segs.e: Kassapa teaches Dhamma to others with the thought:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhīti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Aho vata me dhammaṁ suṇeyyuṁ, sutvā ca pana dhammaṁ ājāneyyuṁ, ājānitvā ca pana tathattāya paṭipajjeyyun’ti.
segs.e: Oh! May they listen to the teaching from me. When they’ve heard it, may they understand the teaching and practice accordingly.’

segs.p: Iti dhammasudhammataṁ paṭicca paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti, kāruññaṁ paṭicca anuddayaṁ paṭicca anukampaṁ upādāya paresaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: Thus he teaches others because of the clear rightness of the teaching, out of compassion, kindness, and sympathy.

segs.p: Kassapena vā hi vo, bhikkhave, ovadissāmi yo vā panassa kassapasadiso, ovaditehi ca pana vo tathattāya paṭipajjitabban”ti.
segs.e: I will exhort you with the example of Kassapa or someone like him. You should practice accordingly.”

segs.p: Tatiyaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 16.4

segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Kulūpakasutta
segs.e: Visiting Families

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ viharati.
segs.e: At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhikkhave,
segs.e: “What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: kathaṁrūpo bhikkhu arahati kulūpako hotuṁ, kathaṁrūpo bhikkhu na arahati kulūpako hotun”ti?
segs.e: What kind of mendicant is worthy of visiting families? And what kind of mendicant is not worthy of visiting families?”

segs.p: Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā …pe…
segs.e: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

segs.p: bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁcitto kulāni upasaṅkamati:
segs.e: “Whoever visits families with the thought:

segs.p: ‘dentuyeva me, mā nādaṁsu;
segs.e: ‘May they give to me, may they not fail to give.

segs.p: bahukaññeva me dentu, mā thokaṁ;
segs.e: May they give a lot, not a little.

segs.p: paṇītaññeva me dentu, mā lūkhaṁ;
segs.e: May they give me fine things, not coarse.

segs.p: sīghaññeva me dentu, mā dandhaṁ;
segs.e: May they give quickly, not slowly.

segs.p: sakkaccaññeva me dentu, mā asakkaccan’ti.
segs.e: May they give carefully, not carelessly.’

segs.p: Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno evaṁcittassa kulāni upasaṅkamato na denti, tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
segs.e: If a mendicant with such a thought approaches a family and they don’t give, the mendicant feels slighted. And they experience pain and sadness because of that.

segs.p: Thokaṁ denti, no bahukaṁ …pe…
segs.e: If they give only a little …

segs.p: lūkhaṁ denti, no paṇītaṁ …
segs.e: if they give coarse things …

segs.p: dandhaṁ denti, no sīghaṁ, tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.
segs.e: if they give slowly …

segs.p: Asakkaccaṁ denti, no sakkaccaṁ; tena bhikkhu sandīyati; so tatonidānaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedayati.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “jiṇṇosi dāni tvaṁ, kassapa, garukāni ca te imāni sāṇāni paṁsukūlāni nibbasanāni.
segs.e: “You’re old now, Kassapa. Those worn-out hempen rag robes must be a burden for you.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, kassapa, gahapatāni ceva cīvarāni dhārehi, nimantanāni ca bhuñjāhi, mama ca santike viharāhī”ti.
segs.e: So Kassapa, you should wear clothes given by householders, accept invitations for the meal, and stay in my presence.”

segs.p: “Ahaṁ kho, bhante, dīgharattaṁ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, paṁsukūliko ceva paṁsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, tecīvariko ceva tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, appiccho ceva appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, santuṭṭho ceva santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, pavivitto ceva pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, asaṁsaṭṭho ceva asaṁsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.
segs.e: “For a long time, sir, I’ve lived in the wilderness, eaten only almsfood, worn rag robes, and owned just three robes; and I’ve praised these things. I’ve been one of few wishes, content, secluded, aloof, and energetic; and I’ve praised these things.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana tvaṁ, kassapa, atthavasaṁ sampassamāno dīgharattaṁ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva …pe…
segs.e: “But seeing what benefit, Kassapa, have you long practiced these things?”

segs.p: paṁsukūliko ceva …
tecīvariko ceva …
appiccho ceva …
santuṭṭho ceva …
pavivitto ceva …
asaṁsaṭṭho ceva …
āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti?
“Dve khvāhaṁ, bhante, atthavase sampassamāno dīgharattaṁ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva …pe…
segs.e: “Sir, seeing two benefits I have long practiced these things.

segs.p: paṁsukūliko ceva …
tecīvariko ceva …
appiccho ceva …
santuṭṭho ceva …
pavivitto ceva …
asaṁsaṭṭho ceva …
āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī.
Attano ca diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṁ sampassamāno, pacchimañca janataṁ anukampamāno:
segs.e: I see happiness for myself in this life. And I have sympathy for future generations, thinking:

segs.p: ‘appeva nāma pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjeyyuṁ.
segs.e: ‘Hopefully those who come after might follow my example.’

segs.p: Ye kira te ahesuṁ buddhānubuddhasāvakā te dīgharattaṁ āraññikā ceva ahesuṁ āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino …pe…
segs.e: For they may think: ‘It seems that the disciples awakened after the Buddha for a long time lived in the wilderness, ate only almsfood, wore rag robes, and owned just three robes; and they praised these things. They were of few wishes, content, secluded, aloof, and energetic; and they praised these things.’

segs.p: piṇḍapātikā ceva ahesuṁ …pe…
paṁsukūlikā ceva ahesuṁ …
tecīvarikā ceva ahesuṁ …
appicchā ceva ahesuṁ …
santuṭṭhā ceva ahesuṁ …
pavivittā ceva ahesuṁ …
asaṁsaṭṭhā ceva ahesuṁ …
āraddhavīriyā ceva ahesuṁ vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādino’ti.
Te tathattāya paṭipajjissanti, tesaṁ taṁ bhavissati dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: They’ll practice accordingly, which will be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Ime khvāhaṁ, bhante, dve atthavase sampassamāno dīgharattaṁ āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva …pe…
segs.e: Seeing these two benefits I have long practiced these things.”

segs.p: paṁsukūliko ceva …
tecīvariko ceva …
appiccho ceva …
santuṭṭho ceva …
pavivitto ceva …
asaṁsaṭṭho ceva …
āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī”ti.
“Sādhu sādhu, kassapa.
segs.e: “Good, good, Kassapa!

segs.p: Bahujanahitāya kira tvaṁ, kassapa, paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: You’re acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Tasmātiha tvaṁ, kassapa, sāṇāni ceva paṁsukūlāni dhārehi nibbasanāni, piṇḍāya ca carāhi, araññe ca viharāhī”ti.
segs.e: So Kassapa, wear worn-out hempen rag robes, walk for alms, and stay in the wilderness.”

segs.p: Rājagahe veḷuvane.
segs.e: Near Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “ovada, kassapa, bhikkhū;
segs.e: “Kassapa, advise the mendicants!

segs.p: karohi, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiṁ kathaṁ.
segs.e: Give them a Dhamma talk!

segs.p: Ahaṁ vā, kassapa, bhikkhū ovadeyyaṁ tvaṁ vā;
segs.e: Either you or I should advise the mendicants

segs.p: ahaṁ vā bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiṁ kathaṁ kareyyaṁ tvaṁ vā”ti.
segs.e: and give them a Dhamma talk.”

segs.p: “Dubbacā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhū, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā, appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
segs.e: “Sir, the mendicants these days are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.

segs.p: Idhāhaṁ, bhante, addasaṁ bhaṇḍañca nāma bhikkhuṁ ānandassa saddhivihāriṁ abhijikañca nāma bhikkhuṁ anuruddhassa saddhivihāriṁ aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadante:
segs.e: Take the monk named Bhaṇḍa, Ānanda’s protégé. He’s been competing in studies with the monk named Abhiñjika, Anuruddha’s protégé. They say:

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Come on, monk, who can speak more? Who can speak better? Who can speak longer?’”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: So the Buddha addressed one of the monks,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena bhaṇḍañca bhikkhuṁ ānandassa saddhivihāriṁ abhijikañca bhikkhuṁ anuruddhassa saddhivihāriṁ āmantehi:
segs.e: “Please, monk, in my name tell the monk named Bhaṇḍa, Ānanda’s protégé, and the monk named Abhiñjika, Anuruddha’s protégé that

segs.p: ‘satthā āyasmante āmantetī’”ti.
segs.e: the Teacher summons them.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” that monk replied. He went to those monks and said,

segs.p: “satthā āyasmante āmantetī”ti.
segs.e: “Venerables, the Teacher summons you.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” those monks replied. They went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them:

segs.p: “saccaṁ kira tumhe, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadatha:
segs.e: “Is it really true, monks, that you’ve been competing in studies, saying:

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti?
segs.e: ‘Come on, monk, who can speak more? Who can speak better? Who can speak longer?’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṁ dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānātha:
segs.e: “Have you ever known me to teach the Dhamma like this:

segs.p: ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadatha—
segs.e: ‘Please mendicants, compete in studies to

segs.p: ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti?
segs.e: see who can recite more and better and longer’?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “No ce kira me tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṁ dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānātha, atha kiñcarahi tumhe, moghapurisā, kiṁ jānantā kiṁ passantā evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadatha:
segs.e: “If you’ve never known me to teach the Dhamma like this, what then do you know and see, you futile men, that after going forth in such a well explained teaching and training you’d compete in studies to

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’”ti.
segs.e: see who can speak more and better and longer?”

segs.p: Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those monks bowed with their heads to the Buddha’s feet and said,

segs.p: “accayo no, bhante, accagamā, yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale, ye mayaṁ evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadimha:
segs.e: “We made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of us in that after going forth in such a well explained teaching and training we competed in studies to

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’ti.
segs.e: see who can speak more and better and longer.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no, bhante, bhagavā accayaṁ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṁ saṁvarāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please, sir, accept our mistake for what it is, so we will restrain ourselves in future.”

segs.p: “Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, accayo accagamā yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale, ye tumhe evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā aññamaññaṁ sutena accāvadittha:
segs.e: “Indeed, monks, you made a mistake. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to act in that way.

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko bahutaraṁ bhāsissati, ko sundarataraṁ bhāsissati, ko cirataraṁ bhāsissatī’ti.
Yato ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikarotha, taṁ vo mayaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma.
segs.e: But since you have recognized your mistake for what it is, and have dealt with it properly, I accept it.

segs.p: Vuddhi hesā, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikaroti āyatiñca saṁvaraṁ āpajjatī”ti.
segs.e: For it is growth in the training of the Noble One to recognize a mistake for what it is, deal with it properly, and commit to restraint in the future.”

segs.p: Chaṭṭhaṁ.

segs.e: “Sir, the mendicants these days are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, bhante, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī natthi kusalesu dhammesu, ottappaṁ natthi kusalesu dhammesu, vīriyaṁ natthi kusalesu dhammesu, paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no vuddhi.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena, hāyati maṇḍalena, hāyati ābhāya, hāyati ārohapariṇāhena.
segs.e: It’s like the moon in the waning fortnight. Whether by day or by night, its beauty, roundness, luminosity, and diameter and circumference only decline.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhante, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu …pe…
segs.e: In the same way, whoever has no faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom when it comes to skillful qualities can expect decline, not growth, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.

segs.p: ‘kodhano purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṁ;
segs.e: An irritable individual is in decline.

segs.p: ‘upanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, bhante, parihānametaṁ;
segs.e: An acrimonious individual is in decline.

segs.p: ‘na santi bhikkhū ovādakā’ti, bhante, parihānametaṁ.
segs.e: When there are no mendicant advisers there is decline.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, bhante, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi kusalesu dhammesu, ottappaṁ atthi kusalesu dhammesu, vīriyaṁ atthi kusalesu dhammesu, paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni.
segs.e: Sir, whoever has faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom when it comes to skillful qualities can expect growth, not decline, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena, vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena, vaḍḍhati ābhāya, vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena.
segs.e: It’s like the moon in the waxing fortnight. Whether by day or by night, its beauty, roundness, luminosity, and diameter and circumference only grow.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhante, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu …
segs.e: In the same way, whoever has faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom when it comes to skillful qualities can expect growth, not decline, in skillful qualities, whether by day or by night.

segs.p: Rājagahe kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: Near Rājagaha, in the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “ovada, kassapa, bhikkhū;
segs.e: “Kassapa, advise the mendicants!

segs.p: karohi, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiṁ kathaṁ.
segs.e: Give them a Dhamma talk!

segs.p: Ahaṁ vā, kassapa, bhikkhūnaṁ ovadeyyaṁ tvaṁ vā;
segs.e: Either you or I should advise the mendicants

segs.p: ahaṁ vā bhikkhūnaṁ dhammiṁ kathaṁ kareyyaṁ tvaṁ vā”ti.
segs.e: and give them a Dhamma talk.”

segs.p: “Dubbacā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhū, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā, appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsanin”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, the mendicants these days are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.”

segs.p: “Tathā hi pana, kassapa, pubbe therā bhikkhū āraññikā ceva ahesuṁ āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, piṇḍapātikā ceva ahesuṁ piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, paṁsukūlikā ceva ahesuṁ paṁsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, tecīvarikā ceva ahesuṁ tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādino, appicchā ceva ahesuṁ appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādino, santuṭṭhā ceva ahesuṁ santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādino, pavivittā ceva ahesuṁ pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādino, asaṁsaṭṭhā ceva ahesuṁ asaṁsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādino, āraddhavīriyā ceva ahesuṁ vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādino.
segs.e: “Kassapa, that’s because formerly the senior mendicants lived in the wilderness, ate only almsfood, wore rag robes, and owned just three robes; and they praised these things. They were of few wishes, content, secluded, aloof, and energetic; and they praised these things.

segs.p: Tatra yo hoti bhikkhu āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva piṇḍapātikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, paṁsukūliko ceva paṁsukūlikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, tecīvariko ceva tecīvarikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, appiccho ceva appicchatāya ca vaṇṇavādī, santuṭṭho ceva santuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, pavivitto ceva pavivekassa ca vaṇṇavādī, asaṁsaṭṭho ceva asaṁsaggassa ca vaṇṇavādī, āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, taṁ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti:
segs.e: The senior mendicants invite such a mendicant to a seat, saying:

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṁ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṁ bhikkhu, sikkhākāmo vatāyaṁ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṁ āsanaṁ nisīdāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Welcome, mendicant! What is this mendicant’s name? This mendicant is good-natured; he’s really eager to train. Please, mendicant, here, take a seat.’

segs.p: Tatra, kassapa, navānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: Then the junior mendicants think:

segs.p: ‘yo kira so hoti bhikkhu āraññiko ceva āraññikattassa ca vaṇṇavādī, piṇḍapātiko ceva …pe… paṁsukūliko ceva … tecīvariko ceva … appiccho ceva … santuṭṭho ceva … pavivitto ceva … asaṁsaṭṭho ceva … āraddhavīriyo ceva vīriyārambhassa ca vaṇṇavādī, taṁ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti—
segs.e: ‘It seems that when a mendicant lives in the wilderness … and is energetic, and praises these things, senior mendicants invite them to a seat …’

segs.p: ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṁ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṁ bhikkhu, sikkhākāmo vatāyaṁ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṁ āsanaṁ nisīdāhī’ti.
Te tathattāya paṭipajjanti;
segs.e: They practice accordingly.

segs.p: tesaṁ taṁ hoti dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: That is for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Etarahi pana, kassapa, therā bhikkhū na ceva āraññikā na ca āraññikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva piṇḍapātikā na ca piṇḍapātikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva paṁsukūlikā na ca paṁsukūlikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva tecīvarikā na ca tecīvarikattassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva appicchā na ca appicchatāya vaṇṇavādino, na ceva santuṭṭhā na ca santuṭṭhiyā vaṇṇavādino, na ceva pavivittā na ca pavivekassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva asaṁsaṭṭhā na ca asaṁsaggassa vaṇṇavādino, na ceva āraddhavīriyā na ca vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādino.
segs.e: But these days, Kassapa, the senior mendicants don’t live in the wilderness … and aren’t energetic; and they don’t praise these things.

segs.p: Tatra yo hoti bhikkhu ñāto yasassī lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ taṁ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti:
segs.e: When a mendicant is well-known and famous, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick, senior mendicants invite them to a seat:

segs.p: ‘ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṁ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṁ bhikkhu, sabrahmacārikāmo vatāyaṁ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṁ āsanaṁ nisīdāhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Welcome, mendicant! What is this mendicant’s name? This mendicant is good-natured; he’s fond of his fellow monks. Please, mendicant, here, take a seat.’

segs.p: Tatra, kassapa, navānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: Then the junior mendicants think:

segs.p: ‘yo kira so hoti bhikkhu ñāto yasassī lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ taṁ therā bhikkhū āsanena nimantenti—
segs.e: ‘It seems that when a mendicant is well-known and famous, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick, senior mendicants invite them to a seat …’

segs.p: ehi, bhikkhu, ko nāmāyaṁ bhikkhu, bhaddako vatāyaṁ bhikkhu, sabrahmacārikāmo vatāyaṁ bhikkhu; ehi, bhikkhu, idaṁ āsanaṁ nisīdāhī’ti.
Te tathattāya paṭipajjanti.
segs.e: They practice accordingly.

segs.p: Tesaṁ taṁ hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
segs.e: That is for their lasting harm and suffering.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, kassapa, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And if it could ever be rightly said that

segs.p: ‘upaddutā brahmacārī brahmacārūpaddavena abhipatthanā brahmacārī brahmacāriabhipatthanenā’ti, etarahi taṁ, kassapa, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘upaddutā brahmacārī brahmacārūpaddavena abhipatthanā brahmacārī brahmacāriabhipatthanenā’”ti.
segs.e: spiritual practitioners have been imperiled by the peril of a spiritual practitioner, and vanquished by the vanquishing of a spiritual practitioner, it is these days that this could be rightly said.”

segs.p: Aṭṭhamaṁ.

segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Jhānābhiññasutta
segs.e: Absorptions and Insights

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ viharati.
segs.e: At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, whenever I want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, I enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedemi, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, with the fading away of rapture, I enter and remain in the third absorption, where I meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, with the giving up of pleasure and pain, and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, I enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, I enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā …pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma anantaṁ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, I enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma anantaṁ viññāṇanti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, I enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati …pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, I enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati …pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, I enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave …pe… saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhomi—ekopi hutvā bahudhā homi, bahudhāpi hutvā eko homi; āvibhāvaṁ, tirobhāvaṁ, tirokuṭṭaṁ, tiropākāraṁ, tiropabbataṁ, asajjamāno gacchāmi, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karomi, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchāmi, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamāmi, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasāmi parimajjāmi; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vattemi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, I wield the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying myself and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. I control the body as far as the realm of divinity.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhoti …pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vatteti.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāmi, dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca.
segs.e: Whenever I want, with clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, I hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati dibbāya sotadhātuyā …pe… dūre santike ca.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāmi—
segs.e: Whenever I want, I understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with my mind.

segs.p: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāmi,
segs.e: I understand mind with greed as ‘mind with greed’,

segs.p: vītarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ vītarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāmi,
segs.e: and mind without greed as ‘mind without greed’;

segs.p: sadosaṁ vā cittaṁ …pe…
segs.e: mind with hate …

segs.p: vītadosaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind without hate …

segs.p: samohaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind with delusion …

segs.p: vītamohaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind without delusion …

segs.p: saṅkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: constricted mind …

segs.p: vikkhittaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: scattered mind …

segs.p: mahaggataṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: expansive mind …

segs.p: amahaggataṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: unexpansive mind …

segs.p: sauttaraṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind that is not supreme …

segs.p: anuttaraṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind that is supreme …

segs.p: samāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind immersed in samādhi …

segs.p: asamāhitaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: mind not immersed in samādhi …

segs.p: vimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ …
segs.e: freed mind …

segs.p: avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāmi.
segs.e: unfreed mind …

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti—
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāti …pe…
avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāti.

Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarāmi, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṁsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi, anekepi saṁvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṁvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe: ‘amutrāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhappaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṁ; tatrāpāsiṁ evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto evaṁvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṁsukhadukkhappaṭisaṁvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, I recollect my many kinds of past lives. That is: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand rebirths; many eons of the world contracting, many eons of the world expanding, many eons of the world contracting and expanding. I remember: ‘There, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn somewhere else. There, too, I was named this, my clan was that, I looked like this, and that was my food. This was how I felt pleasure and pain, and that was how my life ended. When I passed away from that place I was reborn here.’ And so I recollect my many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi: ‘ime vata, bhonto, sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā; te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapannā, ime vā pana, bhonto, sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṁ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā; te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passāmi cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. I understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds. ‘These dear beings did bad things by way of body, speech, and mind. They denounced the noble ones; they had wrong view; and they chose to act out of that wrong view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell. These dear beings, however, did good things by way of body, speech, and mind. They never denounced the noble ones; they had right view; and they chose to act out of that right view. When their body broke up, after death, they were reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.’ And so, with clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. I understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne …pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.

segs.p: Ahaṁ, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: I have realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And I live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.”

segs.p: Navamaṁ.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 16.10

segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Upassayasutta
segs.e: The Nuns’ Quarters

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākassapo sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākassapa was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to Mahākassapa and said,

segs.p: “āyāma, bhante kassapa, yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti.
segs.e: “Come, Honorable Kassapa. Let’s go to one of the nuns’ quarters.”

segs.p: “Gaccha tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, bahukicco tvaṁ bahukaraṇīyo”ti.
segs.e: “You go, Reverend Ānanda. You’re the one with many duties and responsibilities.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And a second time …

segs.p: “āyāma, bhante kassapa, yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti.
“Gaccha tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, bahukicco tvaṁ bahukaraṇīyo”ti.
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And a third time, Ānanda said,

segs.p: “āyāma, bhante kassapa, yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti.
segs.e: “Come, Honorable Kassapa. Let’s go to one of the nuns’ quarters.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went with Venerable Ānanda as his second monk to one of the nuns’ quarters, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhuniyo yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: And then several nuns went up to Mahākassapa, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho tā bhikkhuniyo āyasmā mahākassapo dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.
segs.e: Mahākassapa educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired those nuns with a Dhamma talk,

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo tā bhikkhuniyo dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: after which he rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho thullatissā bhikkhunī anattamanā anattamanavācaṁ nicchāresi:
segs.e: But the nun Thullatissā was upset and blurted out,

segs.p: “kiṁ pana ayyo mahākassapo, ayyassa ānandassa vedehamunino sammukhā dhammaṁ bhāsitabbaṁ maññati?
segs.e: “What is the venerable Mahākassapa thinking, that he’d teach Dhamma in front of the venerable Ānanda, the Videhan sage?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma sūcivāṇijako sūcikārassa santike sūciṁ vikketabbaṁ maññeyya;
segs.e: He’s like a needle peddler who thinks they can sell a needle to a needle maker!”

segs.p: evameva ayyo mahākassapo ayyassa ānandassa vedehamunino sammukhā dhammaṁ bhāsitabbaṁ maññatī”ti.
Assosi kho āyasmā mahākassapo thullatissāya bhikkhuniyā imaṁ vācaṁ bhāsamānāya.
segs.e: Mahākassapa heard Thullatissā say these words,

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and he said to Ānanda,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso ānanda, ahaṁ sūcivāṇijako, tvaṁ sūcikāro;
segs.e: “Is that right, Reverend Ānanda? Am I the needle peddler and you the needle maker?

segs.p: udāhu ahaṁ sūcikāro, tvaṁ sūcivāṇijako”ti?
segs.e: Or am I the needle maker and you the needle peddler?”

segs.p: “Khama, bhante kassapa, bālo mātugāmo”ti.
segs.e: “Forgive her, sir. The lady’s a fool.”

segs.p: “Āgamehi tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, mā te saṅgho uttari upaparikkhi.
segs.e: “Hold on, Reverend Ānanda! Don’t make the Saṅgha investigate you further!

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, āvuso ānanda,
segs.e: What do you think, Reverend Ānanda?

segs.p: api nu tvaṁ bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto:
segs.e: Was it you who the Buddha brought up before the Saṅgha of mendicants, saying:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: ‘Mendicants, whenever I want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Ānandopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharatī’”ti?
segs.e: And so does Ānanda’?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ahaṁ kho, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto:
segs.e: “I was the one the Buddha brought up before the Saṅgha of mendicants, saying:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: ‘Mendicants, whenever I want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, yāvade ākaṅkhati vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharatī’ti …pe….
segs.e: And so does Kassapa. …’

segs.p: (Navannaṁ anupubbavihārasamāpattīnaṁ pañcannañca abhiññānaṁ evaṁ vitthāro veditabbo.)
segs.e: (The nine progressive meditations and the five insights should be told in full.)

segs.p: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, āvuso ānanda,
segs.e: What do you think, Reverend Ānanda?

segs.p: api nu tvaṁ bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto:
segs.e: Was it you who the Buddha brought up before the Saṅgha of mendicants, saying:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: ‘I have realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And I live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ānandopi, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’”ti?
segs.e: And so does Ānanda’?”

segs.p: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
segs.e: “No, sir.”

segs.p: “Ahaṁ kho, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā bhikkhusaṅghe upanīto:
segs.e: “I was the one the Buddha brought up before the Saṅgha of mendicants, saying:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: ‘I have realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And I live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Kassapopi, bhikkhave, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: And so does Kassapa.’

segs.p: Sattaratanaṁ vā, āvuso, nāgaṁ aḍḍhaṭṭhamaratanaṁ vā tālapattikāya chādetabbaṁ maññeyya, yo me cha abhiññā chādetabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
segs.e: Reverend, you might as well think to hide a bull elephant that’s three or three and a half meters tall behind a palm leaf as to hide my six insights.”

segs.p: Cavittha ca pana thullatissā bhikkhunī brahmacariyamhāti.
segs.e: But the nun Thullatissā fell from the spiritual life.

segs.p: Dasamaṁ.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 16.11
segs.e: Linked Discourses 16.11

segs.p: 1. Kassapavagga
segs.e: 1. Kassapa

segs.p: Cīvarasutta
segs.e: Robes

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahākassapo rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākassapa was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando dakkhiṇagirismiṁ cārikaṁ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Ānanda was wandering in the Southern Hills together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa tiṁsamattā saddhivihārino bhikkhū sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattā bhavanti yebhuyyena kumārabhūtā.
segs.e: And at that time thirty of Ānanda’s mendicant protégés resigned the training and returned to a lesser life. Most of them were youths.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando dakkhiṇagirismiṁ yathābhirantaṁ cārikaṁ caritvā yena rājagahaṁ veḷuvanaṁ kalandakanivāpo yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āyasmā mahākassapo etadavoca:
segs.e: When Venerable Ānanda had wandered in the Southern Hills as long as he pleased, he set out for Rājagaha, to the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground. He went up to Venerable Mahākassapa, bowed, and sat down to one side. Mahākassapa said to him:

segs.p: “kati nu kho, āvuso ānanda, atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṁ paññattan”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, for how many reasons did the Buddha lay down a rule against eating in groups of more than three among families?”

segs.p: “Tayo kho, bhante kassapa, atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṁ paññattaṁ—
segs.e: “Sir, the Buddha laid down that rule for three reasons.

segs.p: dummaṅkūnaṁ puggalānaṁ niggahāya pesalānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ phāsuvihārāya, mā pāpicchā pakkhaṁ nissāya saṅghaṁ bhindeyyuṁ, kulānuddayatāya ca.
segs.e: For keeping difficult individuals in check and for the comfort of good-hearted mendicants. To prevent those of corrupt wishes from taking sides and dividing the Saṅgha. And out of consideration for families.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhante kassapa, tayo atthavase paṭicca bhagavatā kulesu tikabhojanaṁ paññattan”ti.
segs.e: These are the three reasons why the Buddha laid down that rule.”

segs.p: “Atha kiñcarahi tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, imehi navehi bhikkhūhi indriyesu aguttadvārehi bhojane amattaññūhi jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttehi saddhiṁ cārikaṁ carasi?
segs.e: “So what then are you doing, wandering together with these junior mendicants? They don’t guard their sense doors, they eat too much, and they’re not committed to wakefulness.

segs.p: Sassaghātaṁ maññe carasi, kulūpaghātaṁ maññe carasi.
segs.e: It’s like you’re wandering about wrecking crops and ruining families!

segs.p: Olujjati kho te, āvuso ānanda, parisā;
segs.e: Your following is falling away, Reverend Ānanda,

segs.p: palujjanti kho te, āvuso, navappāyā.
segs.e: and those just getting started are falling apart.

segs.p: Na vāyaṁ kumārako mattamaññāsī”ti.
segs.e: Yet this boy knows no limit!”

segs.p: “Api me, bhante kassapa, sirasmiṁ palitāni jātāni.
segs.e: “Though there are grey hairs on my head,

segs.p: Atha ca pana mayaṁ ajjāpi āyasmato mahākassapassa kumārakavādā na muccāmā”ti.
segs.e: I still can’t escape being called a boy by Venerable Mahākassapa.”

segs.p: “Tathā hi pana tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, imehi navehi bhikkhūhi indriyesu aguttadvārehi bhojane amattaññūhi jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttehi saddhiṁ cārikaṁ carasi, sassaghātaṁ maññe carasi, kulūpaghātaṁ maññe carasi.
segs.e: “It’s because you wander with these junior mendicants. …

segs.p: Olujjati kho te, āvuso ānanda, parisā;
segs.e: Your following is falling away, Reverend Ānanda,

segs.p: palujjanti kho te, āvuso, navappāyā.
segs.e: and those just getting started are falling apart.

segs.p: Na vāyaṁ kumārako mattamaññāsī”ti.
segs.e: Yet this boy knows no limit!”

segs.p: Assosi kho thullanandā bhikkhunī:
segs.e: The nun Thullanandā heard a rumor that

segs.p: “ayyena kira mahākassapena ayyo ānando vedehamuni kumārakavādena apasādito”ti.
segs.e: the venerable Mahākassapa had rebuked the venerable Ānanda the Videhan sage by calling him a boy.

segs.p: Atha kho thullanandā bhikkhunī anattamanā anattamanavācaṁ nicchāresi:
segs.e: She was upset and blurted out,

segs.p: “kiṁ pana ayyo mahākassapo aññatitthiyapubbo samāno ayyaṁ ānandaṁ vedehamuniṁ kumārakavādena apasādetabbaṁ maññatī”ti.
segs.e: “How can the venerable Mahākassapa, who formerly followed another religion, presume to rebuke the venerable Ānanda the Videhan sage by calling him a boy?”

segs.p: Assosi kho āyasmā mahākassapo thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā imaṁ vācaṁ bhāsamānāya.
segs.e: Mahākassapa heard Thullanandā say these words,

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: and he said to Ānanda,

segs.p: “tagghāvuso ānanda, thullanandāya bhikkhuniyā sahasā appaṭisaṅkhā vācā bhāsitā.
segs.e: “Indeed, Reverend Ānanda, the nun Thullanandā spoke rashly and without reflection.

segs.p: Yatvāhaṁ, āvuso, kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito, nābhijānāmi aññaṁ satthāraṁ uddisitā, aññatra tena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena.
segs.e: Since I shaved off my hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness, I don’t recall dedicating myself to any other teacher apart from the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Pubbe me, āvuso, agārikabhūtassa sato etadahosi:
segs.e: Formerly when I was still a layman, I thought:

segs.p: ‘sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā.
segs.e: ‘Life at home is cramped and dirty, life gone forth is wide open.

segs.p: Nayidaṁ sukaraṁ agāraṁ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṁ ekantaparisuddhaṁ saṅkhalikhitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ carituṁ.
segs.e: It’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness?’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, aparena samayena paṭapilotikānaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ kāretvā ye loke arahanto te uddissa kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajiṁ.
segs.e: After some time I made an outer robe of patches and, in the name of the perfected ones in the world, I shaved off my hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: So evaṁ pabbajito samāno addhānamaggappaṭipanno addasaṁ bhagavantaṁ antarā ca rājagahaṁ antarā ca nāḷandaṁ bahuputte cetiye nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: When I had gone forth, I traveled along the road between Rājagaha and Nāḷandā, where I saw the Buddha sitting at the Many Sons Shrine.

segs.p: Disvāna me etadahosi:
segs.e: Seeing him, I thought:

segs.p: ‘satthārañca vatāhaṁ passeyyaṁ, bhagavantameva passeyyaṁ;
segs.e: ‘Were I ever to see a Teacher, it would be this Blessed One!

segs.p: sugatañca vatāhaṁ passeyyaṁ, bhagavantameva passeyyaṁ;
segs.e: Were I ever to see a Holy One, it would be this Blessed One!

segs.p: sammāsambuddhañca vatāhaṁ passeyyaṁ;
segs.e: Were I ever to see a fully awakened Buddha, it would be this Blessed One!’

segs.p: bhagavantameva passeyyan’ti.
So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, tattheva bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocaṁ:
segs.e: Then I bowed with my head to the Buddha’s feet and said:

segs.p: ‘satthā me, bhante, bhagavā, sāvakohamasmi;
segs.e: ‘Sir, the Buddha is my Teacher, I am his disciple!

segs.p: satthā me, bhante, bhagavā, sāvakohamasmī’ti.
segs.e: The Buddha is my Teacher, I am his disciple!’

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to me,

segs.p: ‘yo kho, kassapa, evaṁ sabbacetasā samannāgataṁ sāvakaṁ ajānaññeva vadeyya jānāmīti, apassaññeva vadeyya passāmīti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya.
segs.e: ‘Kassapa, if anyone was to say to such a wholehearted disciple that they know when they don’t know, or that they see when they don’t see, their head would explode.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho pana, kassapa, jānaññeva vadāmi jānāmīti, passaññeva vadāmi passāmīti.
segs.e: But Kassapa, when I say that I know I really do know; and when I say that I see I really do see.

segs.p: Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: So you should train like this:

segs.p: “tibbaṁ me hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ bhavissati theresu navesu majjhimesū”ti.
segs.e: “I will set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for seniors, juniors, and those in the middle.”

segs.p: Evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: And you should train like this:

segs.p: “yaṁ kiñci dhammaṁ suṇissāmi kusalūpasaṁhitaṁ sabbaṁ taṁ aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi karitvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Whenever I hear a teaching connected with what’s skillful, I will pay attention, apply the mind, concentrate wholeheartedly, and actively listen to that teaching.”

segs.p: Evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.

segs.p: Tasmātiha te, kassapa, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
segs.e: And you should train like this:

segs.p: “sātasahagatā ca me kāyagatāsati na vijahissatī”ti.
segs.e: “I will never neglect mindfulness of the body that is full of pleasure.”

segs.p: Evañhi te, kassapa, sikkhitabbanti’.
segs.e: That’s how you should train.’

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: And when the Buddha had given me this advice he rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Sattāhameva khvāhaṁ, āvuso, saraṇo raṭṭhapiṇḍaṁ bhuñjiṁ aṭṭhamiyā aññā udapādi.
segs.e: For seven days I ate the nation’s almsfood as a debtor. On the eighth day I became enlightened.

segs.p: Atha kho, āvuso, bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṁ rukkhamūlaṁ tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: And then the Buddha left the road and went to the root of a certain tree.

segs.p: Atha khvāhaṁ, āvuso, paṭapilotikānaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ catugguṇaṁ paññapetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavocaṁ:
segs.e: So I spread out my outer robe of patches folded in four and said to him,

segs.p: ‘idha, bhante, bhagavā nisīdatu, yaṁ mamassa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, sit here. That would be for my lasting welfare and happiness.’

segs.p: Nisīdi kho, āvuso, bhagavā paññatte āsane.
segs.e: The Buddha sat down on the seat spread out

segs.p: Nisajja kho maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: and said to me,

segs.p: ‘mudukā kho tyāyaṁ, kassapa, paṭapilotikānaṁ saṅghāṭī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Kassapa, this outer robe of patches is soft.’

segs.p: ‘Paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā paṭapilotikānaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ anukampaṁ upādāyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, please accept my outer robe of patches out of sympathy.’

segs.p: ‘Dhāressasi pana me tvaṁ, kassapa, sāṇāni paṁsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti.
segs.e: ‘In that case, Kassapa, will you wear my worn-out hempen rag robe?’

segs.p: ‘Dhāressāmahaṁ, bhante, bhagavato sāṇāni paṁsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I will wear it, sir.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, paṭapilotikānaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ bhagavato pādāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so I presented my outer robe of patches to the Buddha,

segs.p: Ahaṁ pana bhagavato sāṇāni paṁsukūlāni nibbasanāni paṭipajjiṁ.
segs.e: and the Buddha presented me with his worn-out hempen rag robe.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: For if anyone should be rightly called

segs.p: ‘bhagavato putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo, paṭiggahitāni sāṇāni paṁsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti, mamaṁ taṁ sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: the Buddha’s bosom son, born from his mouth, born of the teaching, created by the teaching, heir to the teaching, and receiver of his worn-out hempen rag robes, it’s me.

segs.p: ‘bhagavato putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo, paṭiggahitāni sāṇāni paṁsukūlāni nibbasanānī’ti.
Ahaṁ kho, āvuso, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: Whenever I want, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, I enter and remain in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected. …

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho, āvuso, yāvade ākaṅkhāmi …pe…
(navannaṁ anupubbavihārasamāpattīnaṁ pañcannañca abhiññānaṁ evaṁ vitthāro veditabbo.)
segs.e: (The nine progressive meditations and the five insights should be told in full.)

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho, āvuso, āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi;
segs.e: I have realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And I live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: sattaratanaṁ vā, āvuso, nāgaṁ aḍḍhaṭṭhamaratanaṁ vā tālapattikāya chādetabbaṁ maññeyya, yo me cha abhiññā chādetabbaṁ maññeyyā”ti.
segs.e: Reverend, you might as well think to hide a bull elephant that’s three or three and a half meters tall behind a palm leaf as to hide my six insights.”

segs.p: Cavittha ca pana thullanandā bhikkhunī brahmacariyamhāti.
segs.e: But the nun Thullanandā fell from the spiritual life.

segs.p: Ekādasamaṁ.

segs.p: Paraṁmaraṇasutta
segs.e: The Realized One After Death

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca mahākassapo āyasmā ca sāriputto bārāṇasiyaṁ viharanti isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahākassapa and Venerable Sāriputta were staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākassapena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Mahākassapa, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Mahākassapa:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso kassapa, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Kassapa, does a realized one still exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “Reverend, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ panāvuso, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Evampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one both still exist and no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Abyākataṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ panāvuso, neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Well then, does a realized one neither still exist nor no longer exist after death?”

segs.p: “Evampi kho, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā:
segs.e: “This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kasmā cetaṁ, āvuso, abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “And why has this not been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Na hetaṁ, āvuso, atthasaṁhitaṁ nādibrahmacariyakaṁ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “Because it’s not beneficial or relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Tasmā taṁ abyākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: That’s why it has not been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Atha kiñcarahāvuso, byākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “So what now has been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Idaṁ ‘dukkhan’ti kho, āvuso, byākataṁ bhagavatā;
segs.e: “‘This is suffering’ has been declared by the Buddha.

segs.p: ayaṁ ‘dukkhasamudayo’ti byākataṁ bhagavatā;
segs.e: ‘This is the origin of suffering’ …

segs.p: ayaṁ ‘dukkhanirodho’ti byākataṁ bhagavatā;
segs.e: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ …

segs.p: ayaṁ ‘dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti byākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’ has been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: “Kasmā cetaṁ, āvuso, byākataṁ bhagavatā”ti?
segs.e: “And why has this been declared by the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Etañhi, āvuso, atthasaṁhitaṁ etaṁ ādibrahmacariyakaṁ etaṁ nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: “Because it’s beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life. It leads to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Tasmā taṁ byākataṁ bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: That’s why it has been declared by the Buddha.”

segs.p: Dvādasamaṁ.

segs.p: Saddhammappatirūpakasutta
segs.e: The Counterfeit of the True Teaching

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena pubbe appatarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni ahesuṁ bahutarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahiṁsu?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why there used to be fewer training rules but more enlightened mendicants?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yenetarahi bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahantī”ti?
segs.e: And what is the cause, what is the reason why these days there are more training rules and fewer enlightened mendicants?”

segs.p: “Evañcetaṁ, kassapa, hoti sattesu hāyamānesu saddhamme antaradhāyamāne, bahutarāni ceva sikkhāpadāni honti appatarā ca bhikkhū aññāya saṇṭhahanti.
segs.e: “That’s how it is, Kassapa. When sentient beings are in decline and the true teaching is disappearing there are more training rules and fewer enlightened mendicants.

segs.p: Na tāva, kassapa, saddhammassa antaradhānaṁ hoti yāva na saddhammappatirūpakaṁ loke uppajjati.
segs.e: The true teaching doesn’t disappear as long as the counterfeit of the true teaching hasn’t appeared in the world.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, kassapa, saddhammappatirūpakaṁ loke uppajjati, atha saddhammassa antaradhānaṁ hoti.
segs.e: But when the counterfeit of the true teaching appears in the world then the true teaching disappears.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, kassapa, na tāva jātarūpassa antaradhānaṁ hoti yāva na jātarūpappatirūpakaṁ loke uppajjati.
segs.e: It’s like native gold, which doesn’t disappear as long as counterfeit gold hasn’t appeared in the world.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, kassapa, jātarūpappatirūpakaṁ loke uppajjati, atha kho jātarūpassa antaradhānaṁ hoti.
segs.e: But when counterfeit gold appears in the world then native gold disappears.

segs.p: Evameva kho, kassapa, na tāva saddhammassa antaradhānaṁ hoti yāva na saddhammappatirūpakaṁ loke uppajjati.
segs.e: In the same way, the true teaching doesn’t disappear as long as the counterfeit of the true teaching hasn’t appeared in the world.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, kassapa, saddhammappatirūpakaṁ loke uppajjati, atha saddhammassa antaradhānaṁ hoti.
segs.e: But when the counterfeit of the true teaching appears in the world then the true teaching disappears.

segs.p: Na kho, kassapa, pathavīdhātu saddhammaṁ antaradhāpeti, na āpodhātu saddhammaṁ antaradhāpeti, na tejodhātu saddhammaṁ antaradhāpeti, na vāyodhātu saddhammaṁ antaradhāpeti;
segs.e: It’s not the elements of earth, water, fire, or air that make the true teaching disappear.

segs.p: atha kho idheva te uppajjanti moghapurisā ye imaṁ saddhammaṁ antaradhāpenti.
segs.e: Rather, it’s the futile people who appear right here that make the true teaching disappear.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, kassapa, nāvā ādikeneva opilavati;
segs.e: The true teaching doesn’t disappear like a ship that sinks all at once.

segs.p: na kho, kassapa, evaṁ saddhammassa antaradhānaṁ hoti.
Pañca khome, kassapa, okkamaniyā dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: There are five detrimental things that lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, kassapa, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari agāravā viharanti appatissā, dhamme agāravā viharanti appatissā, saṅghe agāravā viharanti appatissā, sikkhāya agāravā viharanti appatissā, samādhismiṁ agāravā viharanti appatissā—
segs.e: It’s when the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen lack respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, and immersion.

segs.p: ime kho, kassapa, pañca okkamaniyā dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five detrimental things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañca khome, kassapa, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: There are five things that lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Katame pañca?
segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Idha, kassapa, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, dhamme sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, saṅghe sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, sikkhāya sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, samādhismiṁ sagāravā viharanti sappatissā—
segs.e: It’s when the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen maintain respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, and immersion.

segs.p: ime kho, kassapa, pañca dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”

segs.p: Terasamaṁ.
Kassapavaggo paṭhamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Santuṭṭhañca anottappī,
candūpamaṁ kulūpakaṁ;
Jiṇṇaṁ tayo ca ovādā,
jhānābhiññā upassayaṁ;
Cīvaraṁ paraṁmaraṇaṁ,
saddhammappatirūpakanti.
Kassapasaṁyuttaṁ samattaṁ.
segs.e: The Linked Discourses with Kassapa are complete.
